name: BepiColombo
manufacturer: Airbus Defence and Space / Mitsubishi Electric
best_known_for: Twin-orbiter joint ESA–JAXA Mercury mission — Europe + Japan's first ever Mercury orbiter, splitting into MPO + Mio at arrival in 2026 to map surface + magnetosphere from complementary orbits
credit: Launched 2018-10-20 on an Ariane 5 ECA from Kourou. Mercury Transfer Module (MTM, ion-electric) carries the stack on a 7-year flyby cruise — 1 Earth, 2 Venus, 6 Mercury gravity assists — before Mercury orbit insertion in late 2026. At arrival the two orbiters separate: MPO (Mercury Planetary Orbiter, ESA-built, 480 × 1500 km polar orbit) carries 11 instruments for surface composition, topography, gravity, and exosphere; Mio (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, JAXA-built, 590 × 11 640 km polar orbit) carries 5 instruments for the magnetosphere, plasma, and wave environment. Joint mission rationale: Mercury is the least-explored terrestrial planet; the dual-orbiter architecture covers science neither Messenger nor any single follow-up could.
